alt: A round token of a green-skinned half-orc with short brown hair, amber eyes and two tusks, in a green cloak with silver clasps over a blue tunic, framed by a dark iron rim against a cavern backdrop with glowing mushrooms.
caption: A token saved from the live site: the painted bust in a round iron frame, over one of the ten backdrops, ready for a virtual tabletop.

alt: A painted bust of a human man with swept brown hair, wearing a polished breastplate and gorget under a green cloak with a cowl, fastened with two round metal clasps, on a dark turned pedestal.
caption: Painted, in armour under a cowled cloak. Every garment is grown from the body's own surface, so it fits at any setting.

alt: A painted bust of a red-haired dwarf with a full carved beard, wearing a brown leather jerkin under a green cloak with two metal clasps.
caption: A dwarf in a leather jerkin and a plain cloak. Hair and beards are built over the clothes, so a full beard sits over the collar.

alt: A painted Dragonborn bust with bronze scales in rows, large plates on the head, curled horns, spines along the cheek, a slit-pupilled amber eye and fangs.
caption: The Dragonborn, sculpted by a Blender script and loaded only when chosen. Each scale is its own shade, with larger plates on the head and a paler throat.

alt: The same Dragonborn bust wearing a breastplate and gorget under a green cloak with metal clasps.
caption: The same clothing fits the Dragonborn: a coarser copy of its skin lets the clothes clear its scales.

alt: A grey clay bust of a bearded human in a mail shirt, its surface covered in rows of small overlapping rings.
caption: Mail in clay, as it would print: rows of modelled rings. They are under a millimetre, so they are not yet proven on a print.

alt: A grey clay bust slimmed and scaled down on a tall turned pedestal, standing over a thin orange square drawn under its base.
caption: Preview print at tabletop size: the torso slimmed and the bust scaled to stand inside the one inch square drawn under it, before anything is saved.

alt: A grey clay bust of a human man with swept-back hair, seen from three-quarter view, standing on a round turned pedestal base.
caption: The default bust in grey clay on its printable base. The shoulders are cut flat and the bust stands on a turned pedestal.

alt: A grey clay bust of a bearded dwarf with a ring of dreadlocks and his mouth slightly open.
caption: A dwarf with dreadlocks, a full beard and the jaw slightly open: the model that was printed first.

alt: A grey clay bust of a half-orc with a mohawk, a scowl, the mouth open and a small tusk showing.
caption: A half-orc with the jaw open and snarling: teeth, a tongue and a tusk that turns with the jaw.

alt: A grey clay bust of a tiefling with a swept hairstyle and curled ram horns.
caption: A tiefling with ram horns. Horns come from a handful of generated shapes and are joined to the skull.

alt: Two side sections of a bust through the middle of the face. On the left the underside of the chin is marked red as a flat overhang; on the right a straight sloping wedge joins the chin to the neck and the red is gone.
caption: Why the throat gusset exists: without it the chin's flat underside hangs about 9 mm over air and needs supports; with it the underside is a 45 degree slope that prints on its own.

alt: A black 3D-printed bust of a bearded dwarf with dreadlocks and an open mouth, photographed from the front on its flared round base.
caption: The first print, from the front: face, open mouth and beard came out clean. This is the bust the throat gusset was made for.

alt: The back of the printed dwarf bust. A curtain of dreadlocks hangs down the back of the head; on the left the lock ends are frayed with thin loose strands.
caption: The back. Most locks printed as solid rods, but on the left the lock ends are frayed into loose strands: tips that began with little or nothing under them.

alt: A three-quarter view of the printed dwarf bust showing the dreadlocks ending in a ragged fringe at brow level.
caption: The fringe of locks round the brow ends in a ragged edge. Of the model's 58 locks, 39 ended their tips 3 to 10 mm clear of the body.

alt: A view from above of the printed dwarf bust. The dreadlocks radiate from the crown like a rope-textured pom-pom.
caption: From above: the locks fan out from the crown. Printed bottom-up, every lock that ends in open air has to start its tip on nothing.
